```{r setup, include = FALSE}
has_julia <- nzchar(Sys.which("julia")) && requireNamespace("JuliaCall", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = has_julia)
```

`psnr` generates the sampling lists for collecting cognitive social structures
data: for each person (the perceiver), a stratified set of real and
counterfactual relationships in their social orbit. It calls the Julia package
SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl, which is documented at
<https://human-nature-lab.github.io/SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl>; read its
guide for the procedure itself. This vignette shows the R calls. It needs Julia
(1.10 or later) and is only evaluated when Julia is found.

## Setup

The first time, `psn_setup()` creates a Julia environment for `psnr` and installs
the Julia package into it (a few minutes). The other functions call it
automatically afterwards.

```r
library(psnr)
psn_setup()
```

```{r library}
library(psnr)
```

## A network

A network is a table of ties, one row per tie. Names can be numbers or
strings; they are converted to character.

```{r network}
set.seed(1)
g <- igraph::sample_smallworld(1, 100, 3, 0.2)
igraph::V(g)$name <- paste0("p", seq_len(igraph::vcount(g)))
edges <- igraph::as_data_frame(g, what = "edges")
head(edges, 3)
```

## Lists for every perceiver

With no design given, `psn_sample()` uses the design fielded in Honduras: for
each of degrees 1 to 4, five real and five counterfactual pairs.

```{r sample}
lists <- psn_sample(edges, nodes = igraph::V(g)$name)
head(lists)
table(lists$bin, lists$real)
```

The result is reproducible with `set.seed()`, or with the `seed` argument.

To check or merge with the true network, note that each pair is sorted
alphanumerically in the same way in `lists`:

```{r truth}
truth <- with(edges, paste(pmin(from, to), pmax(from, to)))
mean(paste(lists$from, lists$to)[lists$real] %in% truth)
```

## A different design

`desired` has one row per bin (real, counterfactual) and `dvals` lists the
degrees in each. Consecutive degrees in one element, like `1:2`, are merged
into a single bin:

```{r merged}
merged <- psn_sample(
  edges,
  desired = rbind(c(10, 10), c(5, 5), c(5, 5)),
  dvals = list(1:2, 3, 4)
)
unique(merged$bin)
```

## Consents

`consents` is a named vector of codes (0 = none, 1 = survey only, 2 = survey
and photo, 3 = photo only), with an entry for every node. Perceivers with code 1
or 2 receive a list, and pairs are limited to people with code 2 or 3.

```{r consents}
codes <- setNames(sample(0:3, 100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(.1, .2, .5, .2)),
                  igraph::V(g)$name)
with_consent <- psn_sample(edges, consents = codes)
length(unique(with_consent$perceiver))
```

## Inclusion probabilities

`psn_inclusion_probs()` returns the exact probability, `pi`, that each pair is
on a perceiver's list, with the same design arguments. Its inverse is the
weight for estimation.

```{r probs}
probs <- psn_inclusion_probs(edges)
probs$weight <- 1 / probs$pi
head(probs)
```
